title: Completeness for subideals of the maximal ideal
statement: Let R be a Noetherian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], complete for its maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For every ideal I contained in the maximal ideal, R is I-adically complete.

source.place: Tags 00IP and 0317; the Cauchy-sequence argument written out using Krull intersection.

proof.text: Krull intersection in Mathlib, IsHausdorff.of_le_jacobson, gives I-adic separatedness, since I is contained in the maximal ideal and hence in the Jacobson radical.
Any I-adic Cauchy sequence f is maximal-ideal-adic Cauchy by monotonicity of ideal powers. Completeness supplies a maximal-ideal-adic limit L.

For each n use the finite module Q=R/I^n. For every k put t=max(n,k). The difference f(n)-f(t) is zero in Q. The class of f(t)-L lies in m^k Q. Hence the class of f(n)-L belongs to every m^k Q. Mathlib Krull intersection in the finite module Q makes it zero. This gives f(n)-L in I^n for every n and hence I-adic convergence.
